title: Does a perception-derived target routed into Carnot's value-head-A* explorer convert to discovery? A/B vs the default explorer, 8 games, no LLM.
methodology_note: Both arms = CarnotAgentPolicy(force_explore=True), the LLM-free tier-1 explorer, scored by arc_leaderboard_eval.run_game. Perception arm sets value_head = player->target Manhattan distance (target = nearest non-HUD object to the detected player from a short perceive_entities recon), best_first + navigation_cost_tiebreak=False + value_weight=1 so the value head routes. All in logical grid space. Public-game frames stepped for offline dev validation (authorized), never in the hidden submission.
baseline_context: The greedy-direct discovery A/B (REQ-ARC-WMTE-5834) was 0/8 both arms -- execution was the wall. This tests whether search-based routing toward the perception target breaks that.
mode_robustness_check: depth_first_ride (value_weight 3) also 0 discovery on sc25/ls20/cn04 -- the null is robust across search mode, not a best_first artifact.
diagnostic: The value_head ENGAGES (instrumented: ~41 calls/run, sane distances) but the player->target distance HOVERS at ~9 and never decreases toward 0 -- the search does not navigate the player to the target. Likely causes (not fully isolated): (1) TARGET CORRECTNESS -- the recon picks the nearest non-HUD object to the player as the target, which may not be the true exit/goal; (2) the state-space search does not discover the specific navigation path within budget even with a correct target/heuristic (sc25's win may need a path/mechanic, not Manhattan-greedy movement); (3) the perception arm only ran on 3/8 games (sc25/ls20/cn04) -- the other 5 had no detected player+target in recon, so routing does not even apply.
headline: ROBUST NULL: 0 discovery both arms, all 8 games, across BOTH search modes. Feeding a perception-derived target into Carnot's value-head-routed explorer does NOT convert the perception fix to discovery. Combined with the greedy-direct null (5834), this bounds the result: the perception fix is validated (goal-framing 0->4/8 offline) but NEITHER architecture (greedy-direct nor value-head-routed search) executes it into a solved level out of the box. Execution/navigation is a genuinely hard, separate problem, not cracked by 'route toward a Manhattan target'.
next_investigation: Isolate WHY the search doesn't navigate: (a) verify the recon target IS the true exit (replace nearest-object with an exit-detector, or A/B target choices); (b) instrument whether the explorer's actions actually MOVE the player toward lower distance (is it the search, the target, or the player-movement model?); (c) improve mover/player+target recall so the perception arm covers all 8, not 3.
